newsitem.title: USA: Three die in Texas train collision.
newsitem.headline: Three die in Texas train collision.

text.p: Three people died and two were injured when two freight trains collided head on in southern Texas Sunday night, officials said Monday.
Both trains belonged to Union Pacific, but it was not yet known why they were travelling on the same north-south track, said Union Pacific spokesman Mark Davis.

The collision, which took place on an overpass in Devine, Texas about 30 miles (48 km) southwest of San Antonio, caused an explosion and fire on impact that local firefighters extinguished within 45 minutes.
Some of the 15,000 gallons of diesel oil carried by the two trains was still being cleared from the site Monday, Davis said.
Residents of the area were evacuated for several hours and a highway was closed, Texas Division of Emergency Management spokeswoman Jo Schweikhard-Moss said.
Two of the dead were crewmembers, Davis said. News reports said the third victim was a passing motorist, but Davis said, "We're not sure who that person is."
One of the injured was treated and released from a San Antonio hospital Monday. The other, also in a San Antonio hospital, was burned and in serious condition, Davis said.
Union Pacific crews were working to repair the track and bridge damaged by the collision with the expectation they would complete the job by Tuesday, he said.
Davis said six locomotives and 23 train cars carrying rock and auto parts were derailed. "A lot of the debris is stacked up against both sides of the bridge," he said.
One train was en route from Chicago to Mexico, the other from Laredo, Texas to Baton Rouge, La.
